title: CRAN failure
description:
Unfortunately the recent waldo release broke your package on CRAN because it no longer imports tibble, and your package was implicitly depending on it. The easiest fix is to just make the dependency explicit, by adding tibble to Suggests.

Many apologies for the hassle. Unfortunately we didn't discover this prior to CRAN release because we had a bug in the code that runs our revdep checks 🙁.

title: Overflow error with locale
description:
I did a bit more digging to find out that https://github.com/rstudio/gt/issues/1481 is actually a bigD issue. Maybe related to https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=18618


Here is a reprex

``` r
library(bigD)
withr::with_locale(
  c("LC_TIME" = "en_CA"),
  fdt(
    input = "2021-01-09 16:32(America/Toronto)",
    format = flex_t12_lst$hms
  )
)
#> [1] "4:32:00 PM"
```

``` r
withr::with_locale(
  c("LC_TIME" = "fr_CA"),
  fdt(
    input = "2021-01-09 16:32(America/Toronto)",
    format = flex_t12_lst$hms
  )
)
#> Error in format.POSIXlt(as.POSIXlt(x, tz), format, usetz, ...): output string exceeded 2048 bytes
```

``` r
# respects locale supplied, so maybe as a workaround,
# gt could set it?
withr::with_locale(
  c("LC_TIME" = "en_CA"),
  fdt(
    input = "2021-01-09 16:32(America/Toronto)",
    format = flex_t12_lst$hms,
    locale = "fr_CA"
  )
)
#> [1] "4 h 32 min 00 s p.m."
```

<sup>Created on 2024-07-04 with [reprex v2.1.0](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

Possibly gt should set the option before attempting to do it.

test case can be

```r
# compare output of this test vs the other one.
test_that("fdt() works with non-standard locale when LC_TIME = 'en_CA' (#11).", {
  withr::local_locale("LC_TIME" = "en_CA")
  expect_no_error(
    res0 <- fdt(
      input = "2021-01-09 16:32(America/Toronto)",
      format = flex_t12_lst$hms,
      locale = "en"
    )
  )
  expect_no_error(
    res1 <- fdt(
      input = "2021-01-09 16:32(America/Toronto)",
      format = flex_t12_lst$hms,
      locale = "en"
    )
  )
})

test_that("fdt() works with non-standard locale when LC_TIME = 'fr_CA' (#11).", {
  withr::local_locale("LC_TIME" = "fr_CA")

  expect_no_error(
    res0 <- fdt(
      input = "2021-01-09 16:32(America/Toronto)",
      format = flex_t12_lst$hms,
    )
  )
  expect_no_error(
    res1 <- fdt(
      input = "2021-01-09 16:32(America/Toronto)",
      format = flex_t12_lst$hms,
      locale = "en"
    )
  )
})
```

title: Should `use_tz` adjust the input time?
description:
## Prework

* [x] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/rstudio/bigD/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
* [x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/rstudio/bigD/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue.
* [x] Post a [minimal reproducible example](https://www.tidyverse.org/help/) so the maintainer can troubleshoot the problems you identify. A reproducible example is:
    * [x] **Runnable**: post enough R code and data so any onlooker can create the error on their own computer.
    * [x] **Minimal**: reduce runtime wherever possible and remove complicated details that are irrelevant to the issue at hand.
    * [x] **Readable**: format your code according to the [tidyverse style guide](https://style.tidyverse.org/).

## Description

I was expecting that `use_tz` would translate the input time into the timezone provided to `use_tz`, but it seems to not be having an effect.

## Reproducible example

``` r
dt <- withr::with_timezone("UTC", Sys.time())
attr(dt, "tzone") <- "UTC"

strftime(dt, "%F %T", tz = "UTC")
#> [1] "2023-03-22 13:55:52"
strftime(dt, "%F %T", tz = "America/New_York")
#> [1] "2023-03-22 09:55:52"

bigD::fdt(dt)
#> [1] "2023-03-22T13:55:52Z"
bigD::fdt(dt, use_tz = "America/New_York")
#> [1] "2023-03-22T13:55:52Z"
```

## Expected result

I was expecting the output of `fdt()` to use the `America/New_York` timezone without me having to adjust the input time object.

```r
attr(dt, "tzone") <- "America/New_York"
bigD::fdt(dt)
#> [1] "2023-03-22T09:55:52-04:00"
```
